messages:
michael.k: quick follow-up to the weights-loading RFC — we need to pick a direction for the on-disk layout and warmup path. do we standardize around safetensors + mmap-first, or support a hybrid streaming fallback?

sarah.t: my vote is safetensors+mmap as primary. zero-copy is huge for startup latency. but we have to be explicit about alignment and dtype layout.

ajay.p: agree on mmap benefits, but note: not all customers can mmap from network filesystems. fallback streaming matters. can we design a manifest that supports both? :thinking_face: 

lina.w: +1. propose manifest contains per-tensor file, offset, length, dtype, quant meta. loader can choose: mmap if local and aligned; otherwise async prefetch + pinned memcpy to GPU.

michael.k: rough sketch of manifest (not full JSON, just example format):

```
# manifest
version: 1
shards:
  - path: model-0001.safetensors
    tensors:
      - name: "transformer.wte"
        offset: 0
        length: 12345678
        dtype: f32
      - name: "layer1.attn.k"
        offset: 12345678
        length: 2345678
        dtype: q4_0
# quant metadata: group_size=128, zero_point=..., scale_table=...
```

ajay.p: that looks fine. important: quantized tensors need unpack/transpose rules documented. also need checksums per tensor for partial-shard validation. if a shard upload is corrupt, loader should fail fast.

loader-bot: uploaded checkpoint v2 -> shards: model-0001.safetensors, model-0002.safetensors (sha256 ok).

lina.w: warmup path idea: two-phase. phase 1: metadata-only scan to build plan (which tensors map to GPU/CPU, contiguous ranges). phase 2: prioritized async prefetch: critical tensors (embedding + first few layers) first, rest streamed lazily.

michael.k: exact policy: if mmap allowed and file is local -> mmap and pinned-mem copy to GPU only for quant decode path. else: read via async io into pinned buffer, decode, push to GPU. both should expose progress events to console.

sarah.t: tradeoffs: mmap + on-demand decode reduces peak host memory but can be a perf cliff if many random page faults. need heuristics: if access pattern is streaming (autoregressive) then do streaming prefetch and arrange physical layout by access order during export.

ajay.p: export-time layout optimization is interesting: add optional `layout_hint` in manifest (e.g., token-pos-major) so exporters can compact hot-prefix tensors together. this helps HDD/remote read.

lina.w: regarding quant formats — support grouped-quant and flexible block sizes. loader API should have pluggable quant-decoder interface: register_decoder("q4_0", fn) so runtime can load custom decoders (fast CPU, GPU kernels).

michael.k: API proposal (pseudo):
```
Loader.open(manifest_path, options={mmap_prefer:true, async_prefetch:true}) -> Checkpoint
cp.load_tensor(name, target_device="cuda:0", priority=HIGH) -> Future
cp.stream_iter(prefixes) -> async iterator of decoded tensors
```

ajay.p: add `validate_mode` flag: none/quick/full. full does per-tensor checksum, slow but safe for enterprise.

sarah.t: testing matrix: local mmap vs remote s3-fuse vs s3 stream, for fp32, q4, q2. benchmark cold-start (0->ready), and steady-state throughput for chat style. need to put numbers in the RFC.

lina.w: ops to split across PRs: 1) manifest proto + validator, 2) mmap-first loader with fallback streaming, 3) quant-decoder plugin surface + one reference decoder for q4_0, 4) exporter changes to write layout_hint and group quant metadata, 5) perf tests + CI.

michael.k: timeline? aim for MVP (1,2,3 minimal) in 3 weeks, exporter + perf in 6. ops owners?

ajay.p: I'll take (1) and (3) — manifest proto and a q4_0 decoder reference.

lina.w: I can own (2) and the async prefetch implementation.

sarah.t: I'll do (4) exporter changes and perf harness with tests.

michael.k: ok assigned. one more: be careful about mmap + large-file mapping and address space on 32-bit hosts (rare) but call it out. also ensure we provide clear errors and fallback (streaming).

ajay.p: note: on CUDA pinned memory -> cudaHostAlloc for streaming path. measure copy vs page-locked benefits.

lina.w: question: do we allow mixing formats in one checkpoint? e.g., some tensors as safetensors, some as raw mmap-able bin. pros: smooth migration. cons: complexity.

sarah.t: I'd allow mixed as long as manifest canonicalizes. loader decides per-file strategy. keep exporter ergonomics simple though.

michael.k: action items: write brief RFC addendum capturing manifest sample, loader API, warmup policy heuristics, and test matrix. @ajay.p @lina.w @sarah.t please add perf targets (cold start < 3s for small 2B models on dedicated infra?) and we'll iterate.

ajay.p: noted. will push a draft later today. :rocket:

lina.w: will start an implementation branch and link here.

michael.k: thanks. if anyone spots edge-cases (NFS mmap weirdness, cross-device pinned mem limits) ping here. closing the thread after RFC addendum is posted. :white_check_mark:
